newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Several dead in Pakistan building collapse.
newsitem.headline: Several dead in Pakistan building collapse.

text.p: Several people were killed and at least nine injured when a half-built block of flats collapsed in the southern Pakistani port city of Karachi on Wednesday, rescue workers said.
They said two bodies had been recovered from the rubble of the flattened four-storey building and a number of crushed corpses were visible. Nine injured men had been rescued.
Fire brigade workers said they had heard trapped people screaming for help amid the rubble of the Faiza Heights apartment block in the New Karachi district.
"We can see some bodies crushed under concerete slabs and entangled in twisted iron bars but at the moment our priority is to get the survivours out," a fire brigade official said.
"Concrete fell on top of our floor with a loud bang and we were buried under it," said Muhammad Saleem, one of the injured.

Habib Khan, a labourer working in an adjoining building, said he heard a loud bang and cracking sounds as the apartment block collapsed a few hundred metres (yards) from where he was taking his lunch.
Ambulance workers said earlier that labourers working on the apartment block were having lunch on the second floor of the building when it collapsed. They said as many as 45 might have been buried.

Police, ambulance volunteers and municipal workers searched through the rubble with their hands and crow bars and a crane heaved chunks of concrete out of the way, watched by a big crowd of bystanders.
The cause of the disaster was not immediately clear.
The official news agency APP quoted a witness as saying there had been an explosion before the collapse.
But Malik Iqbal, Karachi's deputy inspector general of police, told reporters there was no evidence of an explosion or any other form of terrorist activity.
Iqbal said arrest warrants had been issued for the builders of the apartment block after they apparently went into hiding after the incident.
A senior official of the Karachi Building Control Authority said use of poor building material seemed to be the reason for the structure's collapse.
